title: Pool of Radiance
build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

records.c: POST.COM's entry, from the linker, after a battle and also for a shop, a temple or a treasure the script sets out. Keeps the stack pointer in $03BF to leave by. The item actions offered ($6EF8): READY, TRADE, DROP, HALVE, JOIN and SELL ($7D) when $6DE2 is set; those and ID ($FD) when $6EF6 is set (a shop that identifies and appraises); otherwise all but SELL and ID ($3D). The VIEW screen offers ITEMS, TRADE and DROP ($6EF7 = $1D). Puts in the module's HALVE, JOIN, SELL and ID routines (item_actions $4615-$4618 and $461D-$4620 from item_hooks), VIEW's TRADE money ($4471/$4472 = trade_money) and DROP money ($447B/$447C = drop_money) and the frame routine ($48C8/$48C9 = frame_box).
Not an entry: LIBRARY's jump table at $2C90 jumps to $0803, the third byte of the STX here.

Ages the party by the days gone by (age_party), clears the effects that last only for a fight (clear_fight_effects), sets the DETECT flag (check_detect), clears the main window. Black border and background, red frames ($6E35 = 2), the adventure's glyphs back (restore_glyphs), the frame round the screen (frame_box with the edges at $4835), the treasure's items set out (set_out_items). Then loads character 8, the first monster: none ($6B00 = 0) means no battle was fought, and every member in the party shares (share_all) before the menu.
Not an entry: ANIMATE's code at $840B and $844B refers to $0881, inside the JSR there.

After a battle: puts the area's SECSET back if COMBAT had replaced it (restore_secset). Then every one of the 64 combat entries, from the last: an empty entry or one that is part of a bigger monster ($6C01 bit 7) is skipped. Its side is $6C0C AND $7F (0 the party, 1 the monsters).
A combatant whose condition has bits 7 and 4 both set is counted in side_marked ($2B5D) and gets both bits cleared.
One that fled ($86) counts in fled_count; any other that is down counts in down_count, and in dead_count ($2B70) when it is GONE ($82) or DEAD ($83). A monster down also counts in $6DC8.
One still standing counts in standing_count; a party member (position 0-7) standing gets a share of the experience (party_share) and, for an NPC, may hide some treasure (npc_hides).

The outcome into $6DC7: 0 when someone in the party stands (1 when, as well, some monsters fled); with nobody in the party standing, $80 when none of it fled and $81 when some did. Then the main window is cleared.
$81: THE PARTY RUNS AWAY (message 2) at row 10; the members left behind are lost (left_behind) and the party goes back to DUNGEON at once (leave_to, A = 1).

$80: THE PARTY HAS LOST (message 3) at row 10 and a pause. The menu follows only when a party combatant had condition bits 7 and 4 set (side_marked), or when fewer than the whole party are GONE or DEAD and $6DE6 is set.
Otherwise the game goes no further: a JMP to itself, so a lost battle ends the game here.
Won: THE PARTY HAS WON ! (message 4) at row 6.
A shop or temple ($6DE2 or $6E6C set) goes straight to the menu.
Not an entry: ECL64's code left in the snapshot at $9A9A calls $0969, COMBAT's status_window.
The treasure: each of the seven kinds of money the script set out (TREASURE, $6EE7-$6EF4) is varied (vary_amount) into the pool ($2B19).
Not an entry: set_window's operand ($4862) is left pointing at $0970, COMBAT's window edges.
Not an entry: ECL64's code in the snapshot at $9A97 calls $097A, COMBAT's show_panel.
Not an entry: ANIMATE's code at $84AB and $850B refers to $0981, inside the LDY before it.

The shares: the party's rows ($6E3E) plus the NPCs' extra shares already in shares ($2B79). Then every monster that went down and did not flee (condition bit 7 set, not $86, side not 0, not part of a bigger one) is loaded.
Its experience into exp_total: the value in its record ($6BF7/$6BF8) plus $6BF9 times its full hit points (255 when they reach 256).

A random number from 0 to shares: one below hidden_shares ($2B78) means an NPC has pocketed this monster's loot. Otherwise its money (add_monster_money) and its items (add_monster_items) join the treasure.
A monster in a party position (0-7) is taken out of the party: entry and character cleared.

Experience for the treasure (treasure_exp) and for its magical items (magic_exp), the share worked out and handed out (hand_out_exp), then EACH SHARE IS (message 5), the share, and EXPERIENCE POINTS (message 6).
With $6DA0 set the party leaves after a pause, with no menu; otherwise PRESS <RETURN> OR BUTTON TO CONTINUE (press_return) and the menu.
The main menu. Notes the files in slots 5 (PIC), 13 (BODY) and 14 (HEAD) in slot_files, to show again after VIEW. $6DE3 set throws the items away ($2B28 = 0).

Each time round: the window cleared, the two frames (draw_frames), the party list on the right, the member under the cursor loaded (member_at_cursor), the picture (show_scene), whether the pool has money (pool_has_money).

The menu bar HEAL BUY VIEW TAKE POOL SHARE APPRAISE DETECT EXIT, with the items menu_mask allows for this member, the cursor on the last choice ($2B49). Up and down move through the party (party_cursor); the bar is drawn again when the new member's mask differs (DETECT).
A choice: its routine from menu_lo and menu_hi into the JSR at $0AC3.
The JSR the menu item's routine is patched into ($0AC4/$0AC5).
The low byte of the menu item's routine, written at $0AB7.
The high byte, written at $0ABD.
The menu items' routines, low bytes: HEAL $209C, BUY $0F71, VIEW $4424, TAKE $1734, POOL $1AB7, SHARE $21CD, APPRAISE $1B26, DETECT $18D0, EXIT $0B82.
The menu items' routines, high bytes.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code left in the snapshot at $6707, $67BF, $6881 and $68E1 refers to $0AD4, part of menu_hi.
The main menu bar: nine items and no heading: HEAL, BUY, VIEW, TAKE, POOL, SHARE, APPRAISE, DETECT, EXIT.

TAKE money: TREASURE AVAILABLE (message $10) at row 2, the pool's amounts (show_pool) beside the kinds there are (the vertical menu money_menu), and WEIGHT LEFT YOU CAN CARRY : (message $18) with how many more coins the member can carry (room_left). A kind chosen: the pool copied to $6D67, TAKE HOW MUCH (ask_amount, $6D62 = 0), then the coins move (take_coins). EXIT or the left arrow returns.

EXIT. Money in the pool, or items left anywhere but a shop: THERE IS STILL TREASURE LEFT (message 7) at row 10 and the bar GO BACK LEAVE TREASURE; GO BACK returns to the menu. Otherwise, or LEAVE TREASURE: leave.
Leaves for DUNGEON (leave_to, A = 1) and drops the stack back to $03BF, so the RTS returns to the linker.
The menu bar for treasure left: two items, no heading: GO BACK, LEAVE TREASURE.
One share of the experience: exp_total divided by standing_count, the 24-bit total in steps (65535 divided again for each count in its top byte), into exp_share. Half of it in npc_exp_share.
Each party member that shares (party_share) gets exp_share, or the half share for an NPC ($6BB8 bit 7), through add_exp.
Adds experience A, X, Y (low first) to the member, after the class's adjustments (class_exp), into $6BE8-$6BEA, at most 16,777,215.
The monster's seven kinds of money, each varied (vary_amount), added to the pool, at most 65535 of each.
Not an entry: print_line_here in COMBAT3 ($7AAC) reads the adventure module's table at $0CAD.
Varies an amount (A low, X high): a d100 roll as a percentage of it, plus half of it rounded up. So 51 to 150 per cent, at most 65535.
Not an entry: print_line_here ($7AB1) reads the adventure module's high-byte table at $0CD5.
Not an entry: ECL64's code in the snapshot at $9AA3 calls $0CFE, COMBAT's apply_damage.

Experience for the treasure in the pool: one point for every 200 copper, 20 silver and 2 electrum (the divisors at coin_exp_div), one for each gold piece, 5 for each platinum and 250 for each gem (coin_exp_mul), and 2,200 for each piece of jewelry (its count's low byte).
Not an entry: ECL64's code in the snapshot at $9A87 calls $0D63, COMBAT's report_attack.
Not an entry: ECL64's code in the snapshot at $9AC4 calls $0D95, COMBAT's report_result.
How much copper, silver and electrum make one experience point: 200, 20, 2.
Experience points for each gold piece, platinum piece and gem: 1, 5, 250.
Adds A (low) and X (high) to exp_total, at most $FFFFFF.

The monster's items join the treasure, the last first: each one's readied flag cleared, merged into a pile of the same already in the treasure (merge_pile) or copied to the end of the list at $9900, until there are 255.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code in the snapshot at $6884 refers to $0DE2, COMBAT's show_moves_left.

After THE PARTY RUNS AWAY, each party member: one under a charm (timed effect 11) loses the effect and leaves the party; one that is OK or fled ($81, $86) is set OK (1); any other, down where it fell, leaves the party too, unless $6DE6 is set.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code in the snapshot at $6571 and $66B3 refers to $0DF9, inside the LDA before it.
No code in the game's files calls this: leaves for DUNGEON (leave_to with A = 1).
The two frames: the bottom panel (columns 0-39, rows 16-23, the edges at $0E57) and the party list's (columns 16-39, rows 0-16, at $0E5B).
The frames' edges: left column, top row, right column, bottom row, for each.
Prints message X at the start of the next row ($03CD + 1).
Prints message X at row A and the text window's left edge.
Prints message X at row A, column Y.
Prints message X at the cursor: its address from msg_lo ($2A8D) and msg_hi ($2AC5).
The vertical menu of money kinds: eight items at column 2 from row 4: COPPER, SILVER, ELECTRUM, GOLD, PLATINUM, GEMS, JEWELRY, EXIT.
The menu mask for money_menu: a bit for each kind the pool holds any of, and EXIT always.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code in the snapshot at $68FA refers to $0ECE, COMBAT's take_step.
From row 4, at column 11, the amount of each kind the pool holds (the kinds pool_mask allows), one row each. Returns the mask in A.

The treasure's items, kept at $9900, 16 bytes each, their count in item_count. $6EF5, from the script's TREASURE, below $80: that ITEMFILE is loaded over $9900 (cleared to $A8FF first) into slot 24, the slot is marked to load again ($6E2B = $FF), and its items are counted up to the first empty one. Then random items (random_items) and $6EF5 = $FF, so the treasure is set out once.
BUY in a shop, and TAKE's ITEMS elsewhere: nothing when there are no items. The frame round the screen, the first page of up to 16 items (first_page).
Each time round: the page listed (list_items) with prices in a shop, and the bar ITEMS: NEXT PREVIOUS TAKE BUY EXIT with what items_mask allows. NEXT and PREVIOUS turn the page; EXIT returns.

TAKE or BUY: TAKE WHICH ITEM or BUY WHICH ITEM (which_prompt) on the bottom row and a cursor on the list. The left arrow or the list's EXIT goes back to the bar. An item picked ($6D44) is loaded, kept, and must fit (item_fits: fewer than 16 items and within the weight): otherwise CHARACTER IS OVERLOADED (message $0B).

The price: can_buy. When the member's own money falls short, the pool's is added (add_pool) and tried again; still short, all of the member's coins go to the pool (return_pool) and NOT ENOUGH MONEY ! (message $23).

Bought or taken: the item goes in the member's lowest empty slot ($6DE9), YOU NOW OWN A and its name (own_message), the change to the pool when the pool paid (pool_change), the member's money paid as change in a shop (pay_change), the member stored, and the item out of the treasure (remove_item).

With items left: when the list now ends inside the page, the page ends one sooner, a page left empty goes back to the first page, and EXIT and the cursor move up a row. The page shown again and the cursor back on it.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code left in the snapshot at $685A refers to $1080, COMBAT's note_attack.
The bar ITEMS: five items: NEXT, PREVIOUS, TAKE, BUY, EXIT.
The prompt for picking: message $1B (TAKE WHICH ITEM), or $22 (BUY WHICH ITEM) in a shop.
The page starts at item 0 ($2B29) and ends at 16 or the last item ($2B2A).
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6787 and ECL64's at $9900 refer to $10B7, COMBAT's show_combatant.
The ITEMS: bar's mask: TAKE and EXIT; NEXT when the page ends before the last item, PREVIOUS when it starts after the first; in a shop BUY instead of TAKE.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $676A, $6857 and $68AB refers to $10C7, COMBAT's face_target.
The page starts where it ended and runs 16 items on, or to the last.
The page starts 16 items back (at 0 at least) and runs 16 on.
Treasure item A's address, $9900 plus 16 times A, into $3B/$3C.
Treasure item $6D44 into the item in hand.
Treasure item A into the item in hand ($6D7C, 16 bytes).
The item in hand into treasure item $6D44.
The item in hand into treasure item A.

Lists the page: the window cleared, then from row 4, column 2, each item's name, recorded as a menu item (column, row, width to column 39, and its number in the treasure as its key), in a shop with its price at column 34 (item_price). EXIT on the row after, then the list's menu kept (save_list_menu).
Never reached, after the JMP: the bytes of a JSR $111A (load_treasure_item).
Elsewhere than a shop: takes item $6D44 out of the treasure, the items after it moved down one place and the count one less. A shop's stock stays as it is.
pool_money_flag = 1 when the pool holds any money or gems or jewelry, else 0.

Gives the member the amount chosen ($6D75/$6D76) of kind $6D66, and the pool keeps the rest of the copy at $6D67. The amount cleared, the member's figures and weight worked out again, the member stored, the menu bar cleared.

Experience A, X, Y (low first) for the member's class: about 10 per cent more for a single class with a high prime ability (prime_bonus), then halved for a character of two classes and a third for three (class_count). Returned in A, X, Y.
Not an entry: ECL64's code left in the snapshot at $9BBC refers to $1272, inside the STA before it.
How many classes each class number holds, 0 to 16: 1 for cleric, druid, fighter, paladin, ranger, magic-user, thief and monk; 2 or 3 for each multi-class.
Multiplies A (low) and X (high) by $2B3B/$2B3C: a 24-bit product in A, X and Y ($4C, $4D, $2B3D), at most $FFFFFF.
Not an entry: ECL64's code at $9BB9 refers to $12B1, inside the ROR before it.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6944, $6958 and $6A09 refers to $12E3, inside the LDX before it.
Not an entry: SQRPACI01's code at $0685, $0727 and $076A, SECSET64's at $683B and $6939 and ECL64's at $9B83 refer to $12E6, inside the LDY before it.
The member's coins in copper pieces: copper, silver, electrum, gold and platinum, each count times its worth (coin_worth), into money_sum ($2B30-$2B32).
Each coin's worth in copper, 16 bits, read at $1337 plus twice the kind: copper 1, silver 10, electrum 100, gold 200, platinum 1,000.
coin_worth's high bytes are read from here, one byte on.
Subtracts the price A (low) and X (high) from money_sum into money_left ($2B36-$2B38): carry set when the money covers it.
can_pay for a 24-bit price, its top byte in Y.
In a shop: the member's money becomes the change (give_change).

The member's coins are cleared and money_left handed back as platinum pieces, as many as it covers and the member has room for (room_left), then the rest as gold pieces. What is less than a gold piece is lost. Carry set when the member could not carry it all. So every sale or purchase turns the member's copper, silver and electrum into platinum and gold.
The price in gold of the item in hand: its worth ($6D87/$6D88) times its count when it has one, times the shop's price factor ($6E6D, 16 for the usual price), divided by 16; at least 1.
In a shop: carry set when the member's money covers the item's price (item_price, times 200 for copper). Elsewhere carry set at once: taking costs nothing.
Keeps the list's menu: the item count with EXIT ($2B40), the menu kind vertical ($6E94 = 0), and the 80 bytes of menu tables ($6E96-$6EE5) copied to $9800.
Puts the list's menu back from $9800, with its count and kind.
YOU NOW OWN A (message $24) at row 10 and the item's name on the next row: for a pile of two or more the line stops one letter short, before the "A". Then a pause.

Counts the coins of kind X (0 gold, 1 platinum) that money_left pays for into $2B39/$2B3A, no more than the room in $6D63/$6D64, taking each one's worth (coin_value_lo, coin_value_hi) off money_left. Carry clear when the money ran out (money_left is then one coin below zero), carry set when the room did.
A gold piece's and a platinum piece's worth in copper, 200 and 1,000: the low bytes.
Their high bytes.

Leaves POST.COM for module A ($6E11): the party settled after the battle (settle_party), the characters of empty party slots cleared (clear_empty_slots), the shop, temple and treasure settings reset ($6E6C, $6EF6, $6E70-$6E72, $6DD2, $6DD3, $6DE2, $6DE3 and $6DE6 to 0, the price factor $6E6D to 16), the screen redrawn with the party list, the area's script marked to load again ($6E1B = $6DA9 with bit 7 set) and ONWARD BOUND ... (message $37) at row 18.

Each party member: a charm on it (timed effect 11) ends and the computer no longer runs it ($6C0C = 0). One unconscious ($85) with hit points, and one OK ($81) or fled ($86), is OK again (1); one dying ($84) becomes unconscious ($85), and one unconscious gets 1 hit point when $6DE6 is set.

For an item with a count, such as arrows: looks through the treasure, the last first, for the same item in all but its count, and adds this count to it when the sum stays under 101. Carry set when merged; otherwise the item is back in hand and carry clear.
Experience for magical treasure: 400 points for each plus ($6D80, 1 to 127) of every item in the list. None in a shop, nor with $6DE3 set.
For a cleric, fighter, magic-user or thief of a single class with 16 or more in the class's prime ability (prime_ability): the experience in $2B2D-$2B2F gets about a tenth more, at most $FFFFFF.

Each class's prime ability, as its offset in the character's record ($6B00 plus it): WIS ($16) for a cleric, STR ($14) for a fighter, INT ($15) for a magic-user, DEX ($17) for a thief, 0 for none. It is read for class numbers 0 to 16, so it runs on into the zeros at $164A.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6870 refers to $164A. The five zeros here end prime_ability; the six after them nothing in this module reads.

Puts back three glyphs of the character set in RAM under the I/O at $D000, which the battle's graphics had replaced: character 0 from glyph_0, character 27 ($D0D8) from glyph_27 and character 36 ($D120) from glyph_36. RAM is switched in for it (all_ram) and back out.
Character 0's eight rows of pixels, which frame_box puts at a frame's corners: a light figure on a solid square.
Character 27's eight rows of pixels.
Character 36's eight rows of pixels.
Draws a box from the edges at A (low) and X (high) (draw_box), then character 0 in yellow at its four corners (corner_marks), and the text colour back ($6E34).
Puts character 0 on row A at the box's left and right columns.

When slot 3 holds SECSET64 (file $64), COMBAT's graphics: the area's SECSET, which COM.PREP kept at $E400, is copied back to $6500 ($600 bytes, copy_memory), and slot 3's file number and the three WALLSET slots ($6E22-$6E24) are put back from $6E83-$6E86, the picture switches ($49FF) from $6E87.

The main menu's mask for the member in hand, in A ($48F9 = $FF lets EXIT through): BUY, VIEW, POOL and APPRAISE to start, TAKE and SHARE when the pool has money. In a shop: no BUY when there is nothing to sell, no APPRAISE unless $6EF6 is set. At a temple ($6DE2): HEAL instead of BUY. After a battle or a treasure: no HEAL, BUY or APPRAISE; DETECT when the member can cast DETECT MAGIC (can_detect), TAKE when there are items.
TAKE. In a shop, or with no items, the money (take_money); with items and no money in the pool, the items (buy_items); with both, the bar TAKE: MONEY ITEMS EXIT.
The bar TAKE: three items: MONEY, ITEMS, EXIT.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6533 refers to $1763, inside the bar's text.
When the pool has money: its copper to platinum is added to the member's coins, at most 65535 of each, so that the member can pay with it (pool_lent = 1).

After a purchase that failed with the pool's help: all of the member's coins, copper to platinum, go to the pool in place of what it held, and the member has none. Since add_pool had added the pool to the member's own, the member's own coins end up in the pool too.

After a purchase the pool helped pay for: the member's coins and the pool's copper to platinum are cleared, and money_left goes back to the pool as platinum and then gold pieces, with no limit of room. Anything less than a gold piece is lost.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6580 refers to $17EF, inside the STA before it.
The bar PRESS <RETURN> OR BUTTON TO CONTINUE, and a wait for RETURN or the button.
Its bar: one item and no heading.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $677A refers to $183D, inside the bar's text.
Not an entry: SQRPACI01's code at $06F8 and SECSET64's at $672D refer to $184D, near the end of the bar's text.
Notes which party positions hold someone ($2B51); then each character slot 0 to 7 whose position is empty has its first byte cleared ($6B00 = 0) and is stored.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $681A refers to $1864, inside the STA before it.
With no battle: every party member gets a share and counts as standing.

Carry set, and bit 7 added to A, when DETECT is not already on ($6DD9), the member can act (condition bit 7 clear) and has DETECT MAGIC memorised (spell 5, the cleric's, or 11, the magic-user's), X its place in the memorised list. Carry clear otherwise.

DETECT: the member's DETECT MAGIC is used up (its place emptied), a timed effect of kind 5 for the whole party for 10 minutes (add_party_effect), the member stored, and the DETECT flag set again (check_detect), so that magical items show a "*".
A new timed effect in the first empty entry (find_entry_x for kind 0): kind 5, on any member ($FF), time A.
Waits for a key or the joystick, the picture animating (animate_frame) once nothing has been pressed for about 50 times 256 passes ($2B72/$2B73), then hands the input to menu_key.
The party member on the cursor's row ($6E36 plus $6D7B) becomes the member in hand ($6EFC) and is loaded.
Sets and clears the main window.
The low bytes of the item actions' routines put into item_actions: HALVE $26AE, JOIN $26DF, SELL $19AA, ID $1D82.
The high bytes of HALVE's, JOIN's, SELL's and ID's routines.
Notes the file number A in slot_files plus X; $FF when it is $80 or more (none, or waiting to load).

An NPC ($6BB8 bit 7) whose byte $6BFA is not 0 takes that many extra shares (its low two bits) into shares and hidden_shares; the lower window shows its name and TAKES AND HIDES HIS SHARE (message $11), and a pause.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6997 refers to $194D, the BPL here.
Waits by the message speed ($49FC).
Shows message X on the bottom row (show_message).
No code in the game's files calls this: the frames and the party list.
No code in the game's files calls this: the combat figures, one column in.
No code in the game's files calls this: the window cleared and the character sheet, one column in.

SELL, an item action. A readied item cannot be sold (not_readied). The name, DO YOU WANT TO SELL YOUR (message $27) at row 4, the item, FOR (message $29), the price (sale_price) and GOLD PIECES (message $2B); the bar SELL ? NO YES. YES: the item goes, the member's money with the price is paid back as platinum and gold (give_change), what the member cannot carry goes to the pool (overflow_to_pool), and SOLD ! (message $28).
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $68F2 refers to $1A09, the JSR here.
The bar SELL ? : two items: NO, YES.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6879 refers to $1A20, inside the bar's text.

An item's sale price: half its worth times its count (one at least), in gold pieces, into $2B41/$2B42 and returned in A and X. money_left is set to the member's money (money_sum) plus the price in copper.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6630 and $6797 and ECL64's at $9AC7 and $9B34 refer to $1A60, inside the ADC before it.
Not an entry: the VIEW screen's SPELLS call at $4480 points at $1A66, COMBAT's view_spells.
With carry set (give_change could not hand it all over): the rest of money_left goes to the pool as platinum pieces, at most 65535, and YOU PUT MONEY IN POOL. (message $2A) at row 15, with a pause.

POOL: the bar POOL MONEY : YES NO. YES: every party member but the NPCs puts all its money, copper to jewelry, in the pool, at most 65535 of each kind. The ADC has no CLC before it, so a carry left set by a kind that reached the limit adds one to the next.
The bar POOL MONEY : two items: YES, NO.

APPRAISE: NO GEMS OR JEWELRY ! (message $2C) for a member with neither. Otherwise its name at row 4, YOU HAVE : (message $2D), the gems' count with GEM(S) and the jewelry's with JEWELRY, and the bar APPRAISE: GEM(S) JEWELRY EXIT with the kinds it has. The piece picked ($2B45) is taken from its count and valued (make_piece). Then the bar YOU CAN: SELL KEEP, KEEP only with an empty item slot ($6DE9). KEEP puts the piece among the items; SELL sells it at the half worth shown (sale_price, give_change, overflow_to_pool). Then round again.
Not an entry: SQRPACI01's code left in the snapshot at $07AB refers to $1B7E, inside the BNE before it.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $682D refers to $1BB4, inside the AND before it.
The member's figures worked out again and the member stored, and APPRAISE again.
Never reached: the bytes of a JMP $1BA6, after the JMP.
SELL: the piece sold at the half worth shown, the money paid back as platinum and gold (give_change) and the rest to the pool (overflow_to_pool).
Two bars: YOU CAN: (two items: SELL, KEEP), and at $1C01 APPRAISE: (three: GEM(S), JEWELRY, EXIT).

Makes the piece being appraised the item in hand: type $46, named GEM or JEWELRY (piece_names), weight 1 and a count of 1. Its worth from the gem table (gem_worth) or the jewelry table (jewelry_worth); then one gem or piece of jewelry is taken from the member's count (take_piece) and YOUR, the piece, IS WORTH and half its worth are shown (show_worth).

A gem's worth in gold: a d100 roll picks 10 (1-25), 50 (26-50), 100 (51-70), 500 (71-90), 1,000 (91-99) or 5,000 (100), from gem_values. Then, while a random number from 0 to 9 comes up 0, the worth doubles.
The six gem worths, low bytes: 10, 50, 100, 500, 1,000, 5,000.
gem_values' high bytes.

A piece of jewelry's worth in gold: a d100 roll picks one of seven classes (1-10, 11-20, 21-40, 41-50, 51-70, 71-90, 91-100), whose dice (jewelry_dice, jewelry_sides) times 100 or 1,000 (jewelry_mul) give it: 1d10, 2d6, 3d6 or 6d6 hundreds, or 1d6, 2d4 or 2d6 thousands. It is meant to double while a roll of one die (jewelry_odds) comes up 0, but roll_die returns 1 or more, so the jewelry never doubles.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6934 refers to $1CA6, the first CMP of the class search.
The doubling loop: roll_die's result is never 0, so the BNE always leaves it.
How many dice for each jewelry class: 1, 2, 3, 6, 1, 2, 2.
What the dice are multiplied by, low bytes: 100 for the first four classes, 1,000 for the last three.
jewelry_mul's high bytes: 0 for 100, 3 for 1,000.
The die rolled for each class's doubling: 9 for the first four, 4 for the last three.
Takes one gem or piece of jewelry (kind $2B45) from the member's count; pieces_left ($2B43) = 1 when some are left, 0 when none.
In a window over rows 21-23 (the edges at $1D7E), YOUR (message $30), the piece's name, IS WORTH (message $31) and the sale price (sale_price: half its worth); the window put back after.
The piece's name word in ITEMNAMES: $65 GEM, $D6 JEWELRY.
show_worth's window: columns 1 to 39, rows 21 to 23.

ID, an item action: costs 200 gold pieces (40,000 copper), from the member's money or with the pool's help; short of it, IT COSTS 200 GP TO IDENTIFY (message $34). Paid: the change (pool_change, give_change), the item's hidden name words shown (bits 0-2 of its flags cleared, $6D82 AND $80), YOU HAVE A ... (message $33) and the item's full name, and PRESS <RETURN> OR BUTTON TO CONTINUE.
Copies A (low) and X (high) bytes from the address in $6E0C/$6E0D to the one in $6E0E/$6E0F, with all of RAM switched in.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6774 and $67CF refers to $1E18, the JMP here.

Each party member who is not GONE ($82): the days gone by added to its day count (add_days), a year of age for every 365 days (count_years), and death of old age when it reaches its race's limit (old_age). Then the days gone by ($49EC/$49ED) start again from 0.
While the character's day count ($6BD1/$6BD2) is 365 or more: 365 off it and a year on its age ($6B74/$6B75).

With bit 7 of $6EF5 set, its low seven bits (1 to 126) are a number of random magical items to add to the treasure, each from the item table (random_base), with a plus (random_plus), a scroll's spell (scroll_spell), bracers' armour class (bracers_ac) and a count for arrows and quarrels (missile_count).
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6852 refers to $1E88, inside the JSR before it.
Empties the item in hand ($6D82 = 4, a name word hidden) and picks a kind from the 36 in the item table by a roll of d188 against their chances (item_chance): its type, name words, weight and worth.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $68C8 refers to $1E9A, the LDA that clears with X set by the caller.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $67CC refers to $1EB3, inside the BEQ before it.
The plus: +1 on a d100 roll of 1-64, +2 on 65-95, +3 on 96-100, as the item's plus ($6D80) and its first name word (+1, +2 or +3, plus_words); its worth is multiplied by it.
Read at plus_words plus the plus (1-3), so the RTS before is never read: the name words $A2 (+1), $A3 (+2) and $A4 (+3).
The plus words random_plus reads from plus_words: $A2 +1, $A3 +2, $A4 +3.
Bracers (type $4D) become BRACERS AC4: plus 6, the name word $DE (AC4), worth 18,000.

A scroll gets one spell of its kind, at random from 1 to 55: a clerical scroll (type $3E) one marked in cleric_spells, a magic-user's (type $3D) one not marked, into $6D89. Its plus word cleared, its flags 0 (the name shown in full), its worth 200.
Arrows (type $49) and quarrels (type $1C) come as a pile of 2d6.

The random items' table, 36 kinds, each column 36 bytes. This one is each kind's chance out of 188: from 6 for a dagger and 15 for a long sword up to 50 for a magic-user's scroll; the last ($FF) takes the five rolls past the rest, the clerical scroll. The cloak's is 0, so none is ever made.

Each kind's item type: daggers, flails, halberds, hammers, maces, morning stars, military picks, quarrels, scimitars, arrows, spears, quarter staffs, bastard, broad, long, short and two-handed swords, composite long and short bows, long and short bows, leather, padded and studded armour, ring, scale, chain, splint, banded and plate mail, a shield, a cloak, bracers, a ring of protection, and the two scrolls.
Each kind's last name word, the one printed first: DAGGER, FLAIL ... RING, MU SCROLL, CLERICAL SCROLL.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6784 refers to $1FCA, inside item_name3.
Each kind's middle name word: ARMOR for the three armours, MAIL for the six mails, OF PROTECTION for the ring, WITH 1 SPELL for the scrolls, none for the rest.
Each kind's weight, low bytes: from 1 for bracers and a ring to 450 for plate mail.
The random items' weights, high bytes: 1 for the five heaviest mails, 0 for the rest.
Each kind's worth in gold before the plus, low bytes: from 120 for arrows and quarrels to 18,000 for bracers.
The random items' worths, high bytes.

HEAL, at a temple: the window cleared and framed, the member's name at row 2, WELCOME TO THE TEMPLE, (message $0C) and HOW MAY WE HELP YOU (message $0D). The temple's code, SQRPACI64 (file $64), loads into slot 1 at $0400, and its menu at $0708 is shown with the mask $FDDF, which hides its two placeholder items, 5 and 9. EXIT (item 11) returns. A cure picked goes in temple_choice; $045E in the temple's code shows its price and asks PAY FOR CURE, carry clear for no; then its routine from temple_lo and temple_hi through the JSR at $20F2.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $678D refers to $20C1, inside the STA before it.
The JSR the cure's routine is patched into ($20F3/$20F4).
The low byte of the cure's routine, written at $20E9.
The high byte, written at $20EF.

The cures' routines in the temple's code at $0400, low bytes: CURE BLINDNESS $05ED, CURE DISEASE $0607, CURE LIGHT WOUNDS $04DD, CURE SERIOUS WOUNDS $04E7, CURE CRITICAL WOUNDS $04ED, item 5 $06D2, NEUTRALIZE POISON $064D, RAISE DEAD $04FB, REMOVE CURSE $0693, item 9 $06D2, STONE TO FLESH $067F.
The cures' routines, high bytes: $04 to $06, in the temple's code.
Adds the days gone by ($49EC/$49ED) to the character's day count ($6BD1/$6BD2).
Each of the 64 timed effects: one of the kinds that last a fight only (fight_kinds) is emptied, and so is one on a combatant beyond the party (its second column 8 or more and not negative).
One of fight_kinds: emptied.
One on a monster's entry: emptied.
The eleven kinds of timed effect that end with the fight, among them $15 (SILENCE 15' RADIUS), $1D (RAY OF ENFEEBLEMENT), $1E (STINKING CLOUD), $33 (SNAKE CHARM), $34 (HOLD PERSON) and $35 (SLEEP).
Death of old age: the character's age ($6B74/$6B75) at or past its race's limit (age_limit_lo, age_limit_hi) makes it GONE ($82), shows its sheet and DIES OF OLD AGE (message $21).
The age at which each race dies, low bytes, by race 0 (a monster) to 7: monster 9,000, dwarf 525, elf 1,600, gnome 750, half-elf 325, halfling 199, half-orc 80, human 120.
Their high bytes, for races 0 to 6; the human's is read from $2195, the first byte of cleric_spells, which is 0.
1 for each cleric's spell number, 0 for a magic-user's, numbers 0 to 55: 1-8, 22-28 and 36-44 are the cleric's. scroll_spell reads all 56, the last two at $21CB.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $6873 refers to $21CB, the last two bytes of cleric_spells.

SHARE: deals the pool out among the party members who are not NPCs, as far as each can carry (room_left, into room_by_member). One coin at a time, round the party in turn (next_with_room), from the jewelry down to the copper; each member's takings are counted at $9700, 16 bytes a member. When nobody has room the dealing stops, and the coin just taken from the pool is lost. Then each member's takings are added to its money.
Not an entry: the frame call at $48C7 points at $21EB, COMBAT's portrait_frame, until postcom_start points it at frame_box.
Not an entry: the VIEW screen's DROP call at $447A points at $21F0, as CAMP left it, until postcom_start points it at drop_money.
Takes one coin of the kind from the pool; a pool with none of it left (kept at 0) moves on to the next kind.
The next member with room, nine tries at most; none, and the dealing ends.
Not an entry: the VIEW screen's TRADE call at $4470 points at $2238, as CAMP left it, until postcom_start points it at trade_money.
The coin counted to the member at $9700 plus 16 times the member plus the kind's offset, and the member's room one less.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $657D and ECL64's at $9A94 refer to $2267, inside the JMP before it.
Moves $6DB4 on to the next party position, round from 7 to 0, Y its offset in room_by_member; Z clear when that member has room.
Each party member's takings added to its seven kinds of money, and the member stored.
Called by the temple's code (SQRPACI64) after a cure: the change (pool_change, give_change), the member stored, its sheet shown, and CURED ... (message $32).

The picture beside the menu: ANIMATE checked in slot 11 and a frame round the picture's place (the edges at $2338). After a battle or a treasure, file 1 into slot 5 (PIC) and the picture shown (start_view_picture, animate_frame). In a shop or a temple, the files noted at the menu's start (slot_files) are loaded back and shown: the whole picture, or a portrait's body and head when there is no picture. Then the keyboard buffer is emptied ($C6 = 0).
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $67C7 refers to $230F, the JSR here.
The picture's frame: columns 2 to 14, rows 2 to 14.

Asks how many of kind $6D65 (A, kind times two in $6D66): TAKE HOW MUCH, DROP HOW MUCH or GIVE HOW MUCH ($6D62 0, 1 or 2, how_much_lo and how_much_hi), the kind's name (coin_names) and the amount ($6D75/$6D76) on the bottom row. Digits type a number (add_digit); the joystick right adds one (one_more) and left takes one away (one_less); DEL starts again from 0; RETURN or the button accepts; the left arrow sets 0 and leaves. The amount is kept within what there is and what the member has room for (most_allowed).
The prompts TAKE HOW MUCH, DROP HOW MUCH and GIVE HOW MUCH.
The three prompts' addresses, low bytes.
The prompts' addresses, high bytes, all $23.
The engine's message for each kind's name, copper to jewelry: 34 to 39 (COPPER to GEMS) and 57 (JEWELRY), through print_message_col.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $679F refers to $2400, the fifth byte of coin_names.
One less, and at 0 the most allowed instead (most_allowed).
One more, and past the most allowed, or past 65535, back to 0.

A digit typed: the first sets the amount; up to four more add to it (the amount times 10 plus the digit); a sixth, or a number past 65535 or past what is allowed (within_limits), gives the most allowed instead.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $67A4 refers to $2466, inside the SBC before it.
How many more coins the member can carry, into $6D63/$6D64: the most it can carry (max_load) less the weight it carries ($6DF6/$6DF7), 0 at least.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $693C refers to $248D, the SBC here.

The amount set to the most allowed: what there is of the kind ($6D67 plus $6D66) or the member's room ($6D63/$6D64), whichever is less.
Carry clear when the amount is no more than what there is of the kind and no more than the member's room.
A short wait (delay, X = $19) after a step of the joystick.

The member's coins to pick from: highlight colour cyan, the frame, the money as the character sheet lists it, EXIT under it (engine message 60), and SELECT COIN TYPE TO and TAKE, DROP or TRADE ($6D62) on the bottom row. Returns the kind picked in $6D65 and A, N set ($FF) for EXIT.
The prompt SELECT COIN TYPE TO , then TAKE, DROP and TRADE.
Not an entry: SECSET64's code at $67C2 refers to $258E, inside the prompt's text.
The three verbs' addresses, low bytes: $25A2 TAKE, $25A7 DROP, $25AC TRADE.
Their high bytes; the two bytes after them nothing reads.
Copies the member's seven kinds of money ($6BBB, 14 bytes) to $6D67.
Copies them back from $6D67.

DROP money, from the VIEW screen: the member's sheet, a kind (pick_coin), DROP HOW MUCH with no limit of room (ask_amount), and that much is taken from the member. The money dropped is gone, not put in the pool.
Takes the amount from kind $6D66 of the copy at $6D67.

TRADE money, from the VIEW screen: TRADE TO ? (trade_to) for the receiver ($6EFD), EXIT going back to the giver. A kind from the giver (pick_coin); GIVE HOW MUCH within what the giver has and the receiver can carry (ask_amount); it is added to the receiver and taken from the giver.
Multiplies A (low) and X (high) by Y: the 16-bit product in A and X ($4C/$4D); anything past 65535 is lost.

HALVE, an item action: an item without a count says THAT CAN'T BE HALVED. Otherwise the pile splits: the larger half stays, and the smaller half, when there is one, goes into the lowest empty slot, not readied.
JOIN, an item action: for an item with a count, every other item the same in all but its count and readied flag is added to it and emptied (join_one), up to 250.
Adds this item's count to the kept item's when there is no carry and the sum is under 251, and empties this one.

THAT CAN'T BE HALVED, shown by halve.

Not an entry: SQRPACI01's code at $0773 and ECL64's at $9B8A and $9BBF refer to $2744, inside halve_message.
